angle_name: Balanced hyperbola wedge and signed renewal contraction
mechanism: Pass from π−Li to the logarithmically weighted Chebyshev measure by Stieltjes partial summation, retaining the weight 1/log and recording prime-power terms explicitly. For u in [(y+1)^2−1−y,(y+1)^2−1], every pair ab≤u has a≤y or b≤y, while the entire rectangle a,b≤y is present. Thus the truncated convolution T_y(u)=Σ_{ab≤u,a≤y} μ(a)Λ(b) admits an exact hyperbola symmetrization. Its symmetric part collapses using μ*Λ=−μ log; the remaining part is the antisymmetric wedge Σ_{ab≤u}[1_{a≤y}μ(a)Λ(b)−1_{b≤y}Λ(b)μ(a)]. Perform the same symmetrization on the continuous centering term before estimating anything. The proposed attack is to prove an L2 spectral gap for this signed wedge-renewal operator on the canonical backward window, then iterate the complementary-scale renewal relation. The μ and prime signs remain coupled throughout; logarithmic weights and prime-power corrections are handled by partial summation and lower-scale copies of the same operator.
new_leverage: This uses the only explicitly live opening in obstacle 9: an antisymmetric, signed contraction rather than an absolute renewal bound. Hyperbola swapping removes the common symmetric mode before Cauchy–Schwarz, so it also exits the F-closure in obstacle 1. The exact square-window geometry makes the swap uniform on the sanctioned pinned window, while L2 control tolerates the Wigert-sized individual jumps from obstacle 8.
target_estimate: Uniform balanced-wedge contraction: after exact Li-centering and inclusion of the explicit prime-power correction P_y(u), prove for some fixed η,δ0>0 that the canonical-window energy of the wedge residual B_y satisfies ||B_y+P_y||_{L2(I_y)}^2 ≤ (1−η)E_recur(y)+Oε(y^(5−4δ0+ε)), where I_y=[y^2+y,y^2+2y], E_recur is the same normalized signed energy at the complementary arguments u/a, and no component is replaced by its absolute value. Iteration would give (1/y)Σ_{t<y}|S(y,(y+1)^2−1−t)|^2 ≪ε y^(4−4δ+ε)=x^(2−2δ+ε). The rung-2 form is the corresponding bound ≪ε y^(2+ε)=x^(1+ε) for the averaged energy.

obstacle_positions.1: The μ×Λ interaction is retained inside an antisymmetric wedge; Cauchy–Schwarz is allowed only after the symmetric zero mode has been cancelled exactly.
obstacle_positions.2: No pair is assigned to a single modulus: the whole shifted-product relation is treated as one bilinear operator, so growing fibers and conductors up to 4D² are not assumed away.
obstacle_positions.3: The argument is restricted to the exact backward windows at (y+1)^2−1, where the rectangle inclusion and hyperbola cover are stable; no generic-x exceptional-set claim is used.
obstacle_positions.4: Only balanced variables and packet-level conductors of the hyperbola operator occur; the enormous full wheel modulus never enters.
obstacle_positions.5: This is not sieve-only: the desired gain is specifically a signed Möbius–von-Mangoldt spectral gap, and removing μ would destroy the mechanism.
obstacle_positions.6: No pointwise estimate for R and no absolute sum over zeros is invoked; any zero-free consequence must emerge from the direct signed contraction rather than be assumed.
obstacle_positions.7: Finite computations are used only to falsify the proposed contraction or expose an uncancelled mode, never to promote it.
obstacle_positions.8: The proof seeks windowed L2 energy and permits large divisor-supported increments; it assumes neither pointwise polylogarithmic smoothness nor bounded jumps.
obstacle_positions.9: The complete convolution identity is used only to cancel the symmetric half; the remaining renewal step is signed and antisymmetric, exactly the case not eliminated by the absolute-mass counterarguments.

kill_test: Derive the weighted identity completely, including Li-centering and every prime-power term, and inspect the q=1/rectangle component. If any uncancelled term proportional to M(y)(ψ(y)−y), M(y), or an absolute renewal mass remains before estimation, the route is immediately killed by obstacles 1 and 6. If the algebra passes, form the finite signed renewal matrix for modest y and compute its norm after removing the exact symmetric mode; a norm at least 1 with an explicit stable arithmetic test vector kills the contraction strategy.
rung1_version: Prove only a fixed spectral saving, for example a wedge-energy bound Oε(y^(5−1/16+ε)); after renewal iteration this is intended to yield the honest deliverable S(y,x)≪ε x^(1−1/64+ε), with constants uniform over all canonical backward windows.
plausible_partial: A Lean-formalizable balanced-hyperbola wedge lemma: throughout the full canonical backward window, prove the exact domain cover, stable rectangle identity, μ*Λ symmetrization, continuous-centering analogue, and an explicit decomposition of the π−Li Abel functional into the signed wedge plus enumerated prime-power and endpoint corrections. This would decisively show whether the proposed contraction has an uncontaminated zero mode.
weakest_assumption: After exact removal of the symmetric convolution mode, the actual Möbius–prime signed renewal operator has a uniform L2 norm strictly below one on canonical square windows; no analogous contraction is assumed for arbitrary coefficient sequences.
